title: Academor SAT Practice Test 3 Reading and Writing

questions.question:
The restorer's work on the damaged painting was ____________: over two years she removed centuries of grime with brushes no wider than a few hairs, checking each section under a microscope before moving on.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Tiny brushes and checking every section under a microscope describe extremely careful, or meticulous, work.

questions.question:
Tiny particles of plastic have become ____________ in the environment: researchers have found them in deep-ocean sediments, in snow on remote mountains, and in drinking water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Being found in places from the deep ocean to remote mountains means the particles are everywhere, or pervasive.

questions.question:
Although the composer's early works followed the conventions of her time, her later pieces were strikingly ____________, using unusual scales and irregular rhythms that puzzled many listeners.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

“Although” sets the later pieces against conventional early works; unusual scales and rhythms show they were innovative.

questions.question:
The senator was known for her ____________ manner: she rarely raised her voice and preferred to win over opponents through patient, carefully reasoned argument.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

A calm, patient, reasoned style is measured; “volatile” is the opposite.

questions.question:
Rosalind Franklin's contribution to the discovery of the structure of DNA was long overlooked. Her X-ray images of DNA, including one now known as Photo 51, provided key evidence that the molecule has a helical shape. Yet when James Watson and Francis Crick published their model of DNA in 1953, Franklin's role received little public recognition.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes an experiment that Watson and Crick carried out to test Franklin's results.
It explains what Franklin contributed, a contribution the text says was overlooked.
It argues that Franklin's images were more important than Watson and Crick's model.
It introduces a disagreement about the shape of DNA that the text goes on to resolve.
questions.correct: It explains what Franklin contributed, a contribution the text says was overlooked.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The first sentence says Franklin's contribution was overlooked; the underlined sentence states what that contribution was.

questions.question:
When a honeybee colony outgrows its hive, thousands of bees leave with the queen and cluster on a branch while a few hundred scouts search for a new home. A scout that finds a promising cavity returns and performs a dance that advertises it, and other scouts fly off to inspect the site. Over hours or days, more and more scouts dance for the best site, until enough of them have gathered there and the whole swarm flies to its new home.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain why honeybee colonies sometimes outgrow their hives
To compare the dances of honeybee scouts with those of other insects
To describe how a honeybee swarm chooses a new place to live
To argue that honeybee scouts often choose poor nest sites
questions.correct: To describe how a honeybee swarm chooses a new place to live
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text follows the process from the swarm leaving the hive to the choice of the best site.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some art historians argue that the bright colors of Impressionist painting were made possible largely by new materials. Paint sold in metal tubes allowed artists to work outdoors, and newly invented pigments gave them vivid colors that earlier painters had not been able to use.

Text 2

Art historian Inès Dubois points out that several leading Impressionists continued to rely on traditional pigments for much of their careers. In her view, the movement's brightness came mainly from the artists' interest in capturing changing outdoor light, an interest that would have shaped their work even without new materials.

Based on the texts, how would Dubois (Text 2) most likely respond to the art historians' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that Impressionist painters could not have worked outdoors without paint tubes
By suggesting that it overstates the role of new materials in shaping Impressionist painting
By claiming that Impressionist painters used only newly invented pigments
By arguing that Impressionist paintings were less colorful than earlier paintings
questions.correct: By suggesting that it overstates the role of new materials in shaping Impressionist painting
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Dubois credits the artists' interest in light rather than new materials, and notes that leading painters kept using traditional pigments.

questions.question:
The narwhal, a whale of the Arctic Ocean, is known for its long, spiral tusk, which is actually a tooth that grows through the animal's upper lip. For centuries, people assumed the tusk was used mainly as a weapon. Some researchers now propose a different main purpose: the tusk contains millions of nerve endings that connect the outside of the tooth to the animal's brain, and they suggest the tusk may help narwhals sense changes in the water around them.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The narwhal's tusk grows through the animal's lower jaw rather than its lip.
Narwhals use their tusks mainly to fight other narwhals during the breeding season.
Researchers have proved that narwhals use their tusks to find food.
Some researchers think the narwhal's tusk may serve mainly as a sense organ rather than as a weapon.
questions.correct: Some researchers think the narwhal's tusk may serve mainly as a sense organ rather than as a weapon.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The text contrasts the old weapon idea with the newer proposal that the tusk senses the water.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Tomas, age twelve, has just lost a chess match at his first tournament.

He shook his opponent's hand without looking up. On the bus home, while his mother talked about dinner, Tomas replayed the game on the small magnetic board in his lap, moving the pieces back to the twenty-third move, where his bishop had wandered into danger. He tried a different square, then another. By the time the bus reached their stop, he had found the move he should have made, and he was already wondering when the next tournament would be.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tomas is so upset by his loss that he refuses to talk to his mother.
Tomas blames his opponent for distracting him during the match.
After losing, Tomas studies his mistake and becomes eager to compete again.
Tomas decides that tournament chess is too stressful for him.
questions.correct: After losing, Tomas studies his mistake and becomes eager to compete again.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Tomas replays the game, finds the better move and looks forward to the next tournament.

questions.question:
Red foxes that live in cities often approach people more closely than foxes in the countryside do. Biologist Megan Holloway hypothesizes that city foxes have become less fearful because many of them are regularly given food by residents.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?
options: City foxes are, on average, slightly larger than foxes in the countryside.
Foxes in the countryside are more active at night than during the day.
The number of foxes living in the city has increased over the past thirty years.
Within the same city, foxes in neighborhoods where residents often leave out food approached people more closely than foxes in neighborhoods where residents rarely do.
questions.correct: Within the same city, foxes in neighborhoods where residents often leave out food approached people more closely than foxes in neighborhoods where residents rarely do.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

This finding links closeness to people directly to being fed, while keeping the city setting the same.

questions.question:
A city planner in Harlow is writing a report on travel times. The planner notes that cycling is the fastest way for many residents to get to work, with an average commute time of ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: 27 minutes, shorter than the average for travel by bus.
41 minutes, the longest of the four travel modes.
22 minutes, about the same as the average for travel by train.
22 minutes, shorter than the average for travel by car, bus, or train.
questions.correct: 22 minutes, shorter than the average for travel by car, bus, or train.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The claim is that cycling is fastest; only this choice gives the bicycle time and correctly says it is the shortest.

questions.question:
Although sales of CDs in Country Q fell steadily between 2014 and 2022, a music journalist argues that interest in physical recordings has not disappeared, pointing out that during the same period ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: sales of vinyl records rose from about 4 million to about 19 million.
sales of CDs fell from about 48 million to about 12 million.
sales of vinyl records were higher than sales of CDs in every year shown.
sales of vinyl records fell from about 19 million to about 4 million.
questions.correct: sales of vinyl records rose from about 4 million to about 19 million.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Rising vinyl sales show continuing interest in physical recordings despite the fall in CD sales.

questions.question:
Researchers measured how quickly drivers in a simulator could press the brake when an obstacle appeared. They concluded that a phone conversation slows drivers more than a conversation with a passenger, even when the driver's hands stay free: average reaction time was ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: 1.46 seconds while reading a text message, compared with 0.71 seconds with no distraction.
0.84 seconds while talking with a passenger, compared with 0.71 seconds with no distraction.
0.98 seconds during a hands-free phone call, compared with 0.84 seconds while talking with a passenger.
0.98 seconds while talking with a passenger, compared with 0.84 seconds during a hands-free phone call.
questions.correct: 0.98 seconds during a hands-free phone call, compared with 0.84 seconds while talking with a passenger.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The conclusion compares a hands-free call with talking to a passenger; only this choice reports those two values correctly.

questions.question:
At a village site about 3,000 years old, archaeologists found hundreds of pieces of pottery. Chemical analysis showed that most pieces were made from clay dug near the village, but about a tenth were made from a clay found only in a valley more than 200 kilometers away. The village shows no sign that its residents ever traveled that far. These findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the villagers may have obtained some pottery through trade with other communities.
the villagers moved to the distant valley after they stopped making pottery.
pottery made from local clay was of higher quality than pottery from the valley.
the distant valley was not inhabited 3,000 years ago.
questions.correct: the villagers may have obtained some pottery through trade with other communities.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Pottery from a distant clay source, without signs that villagers traveled there, points to exchange with others.

questions.question:
The results of the survey, which asked more than 2,000 residents about local parks, ____________ that most people visit a park at least once a week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The subject is the plural “results,” so the verb must be plural: show.

questions.question:
The museum had planned to close the exhibit in ____________ record attendance, the directors decided to keep it open through the summer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“However” joins two independent clauses, so it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

questions.question:
The orchestra announced that ____________ would perform a free concert in the city park on the first Sunday of every month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“Orchestra” is a singular noun here, so the singular pronoun it refers to it.

questions.question:
Kente cloth, a fabric woven in narrow strips by the Asante and Ewe peoples of West ____________ known for its bright colors and geometric patterns.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The appositive that begins with a comma after “cloth” must close with a comma before the verb “is.”

questions.question:
By the end of the nineteenth century, railroads ____________ the time it took to cross the United States from several months to about a week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

“By the end of the nineteenth century” describes an action completed before a past time, so the past perfect had reduced fits.

questions.question:
The recipe calls for three kinds of ____________ cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A colon introduces the list that names the three spices.

questions.question:
Every one of the paintings in the gallery's new wing ____________ been cleaned and reframed before the reopening.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The subject is “every one,” which is singular, so the verb is has.

questions.question:
Sharks have no bones; their skeletons are made of cartilage. ____________ their fossil record consists mostly of teeth, which are hard enough to survive for millions of years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Because cartilage rarely fossilizes, the fossil record is mostly teeth: a consequence.

questions.question:
The early versions of the app were difficult to use. ____________ the newest version, which was redesigned with help from hundreds of test users, has received excellent reviews.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The well-reviewed new version contrasts with the difficult early versions.

questions.question:
The novel is set in a single small town over just three days. ____________ it manages to touch on almost every major event in the town's two-hundred-year history.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Covering two centuries despite a three-day setting is unexpected, which “Nevertheless” signals.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Rosetta spacecraft was launched by the European Space Agency in 2004.
  • It traveled for ten years to reach a comet called 67P.
  • In 2014 it released a small lander called Philae.
  • Philae became the first spacecraft to land on the surface of a comet.

The student wants to emphasize the historic achievement of the Rosetta mission.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In 2014 the Rosetta mission's Philae lander became the first spacecraft ever to land on a comet.
The Rosetta spacecraft was launched by the European Space Agency in 2004.
Rosetta traveled for ten years to reach a comet called 67P.
The Rosetta spacecraft carried a small lander called Philae.
questions.correct: In 2014 the Rosetta mission's Philae lander became the first spacecraft ever to land on a comet.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice states the first-ever landing on a comet.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Bamboo is a type of grass.
  • Some species of bamboo can grow almost a meter in a single day.
  • Oak trees usually grow less than a meter per year.
  • Both bamboo and oak are used as building materials.

The student wants to contrast the growth rates of bamboo and oak.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: While some bamboo species can grow almost a meter in a day, oak trees usually grow less than a meter in a whole year.
Both bamboo and oak are used as building materials.
Bamboo, which is a type of grass, is used as a building material.
Some species of bamboo can grow almost a meter in a single day.
questions.correct: While some bamboo species can grow almost a meter in a day, oak trees usually grow less than a meter in a whole year.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice compares the two growth rates.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Ibn Battuta was a scholar born in Tangier, Morocco, in 1304.
  • Over about thirty years he traveled through North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, and China.
  • His travels covered roughly 120,000 kilometers.
  • After returning home, he dictated an account of his journeys, known as the Rihla.

The student wants to introduce Ibn Battuta to readers who are unfamiliar with him.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ibn Battuta's travels covered roughly 120,000 kilometers.
The Rihla was dictated after Ibn Battuta returned home.
Ibn Battuta, a fourteenth-century scholar from Morocco, traveled for about thirty years across Africa and Asia and later described his journeys in a book known as the Rihla.
Ibn Battuta traveled through North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, and China.
questions.correct: Ibn Battuta, a fourteenth-century scholar from Morocco, traveled for about thirty years across Africa and Asia and later described his journeys in a book known as the Rihla.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice says who Ibn Battuta was and what he is known for.

questions.question:
The historian's account of the strike is admirably ____________: she quotes workers, factory owners, and government officials at length and allows readers to weigh their claims for themselves.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Giving every group a full hearing and letting readers decide is evenhanded.

questions.question:
Although the scientist's early results seemed to ____________ her hypothesis, later experiments with larger samples failed to reproduce them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

“Although” contrasts the early results with later failures; the early results seemed to support, or vindicate, the hypothesis.

questions.question:
The ____________ of the documents surprised the researchers: a single box in the archive contained letters, receipts, maps, recipes, and even children's drawings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A box with many different kinds of documents shows heterogeneity, or variety.

questions.question:
Critics praised the actor's ____________ performance: rather than shouting or weeping, he conveyed the character's grief through small gestures and long silences.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Small gestures and silences instead of shouting show a restrained performance.

questions.question:
For centuries, sailors told stories of “rogue waves,” single waves far taller than those around them that appeared without warning. Many scientists dismissed the stories as exaggerations, since standard models of the ocean predicted that such waves would be extremely rare. Then, on January 1, 1995, a sensor on the Draupner oil platform in the North Sea recorded a wave about 26 meters high in seas where most waves were about 12 meters. The measurement prompted researchers to develop new models that could explain how such waves form.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It explains how rogue waves form and then describes how sailors can avoid them.
It compares sailors' stories with scientific models and concludes that both were mistaken.
It describes a measurement and then argues that the sensor that recorded it was faulty.
It describes a phenomenon that was long doubted, presents a measurement that confirmed it, and notes the research that followed.
questions.correct: It describes a phenomenon that was long doubted, presents a measurement that confirmed it, and notes the research that followed.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The text moves from doubted stories, to the 1995 measurement, to the new models it prompted.

questions.question:
Many people assume that a desert is defined by heat. Yet Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth, is also the largest desert in the world. Scientists define a desert by how little precipitation it receives, and most of Antarctica's interior gets less than 5 centimeters of precipitation a year.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives an example that supports the assumption in the first sentence.
It explains why scientists measure precipitation in centimeters.
It presents a fact that seems to contradict the assumption in the first sentence.
It introduces a claim that the final sentence shows to be false.
questions.correct: It presents a fact that seems to contradict the assumption in the first sentence.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A cold desert challenges the assumption that deserts are defined by heat; the final sentence then explains why Antarctica counts as a desert.

questions.question:
Text 1

Many urban planners argue that building more roads is the best way to reduce traffic congestion. More lanes, they say, give the same number of cars more space, so traffic should move faster.

Text 2

Transportation researcher Kofi Asante studied highways in thirty cities over two decades. He found that when cities added lanes, the amount of driving increased almost in proportion to the new space, and within a few years congestion returned to its earlier level. Asante calls this effect “induced demand”: new roads encourage people to make trips they would not otherwise have made.

Based on the texts, how would Asante (Text 2) most likely respond to the urban planners' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that building more roads is the most effective way to reduce congestion
By pointing out that it assumes the number of cars stays the same after new lanes are built
By arguing that congestion is caused mainly by poorly designed traffic lights
By suggesting that the planners studied too few cities to reach a conclusion
questions.correct: By pointing out that it assumes the number of cars stays the same after new lanes are built
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The planners assume “the same number of cars,” but Asante found that new lanes bring more driving.

questions.question:
For a long time, scientists assumed that plants could not respond to sound. Recent studies have begun to challenge that assumption. In one experiment, researchers played recordings of buzzing bees to evening primrose flowers. Within minutes, the flowers produced nectar with a higher sugar content than flowers that heard silence or higher-pitched sounds. The researchers suggest that this response may help the plants attract pollinators that are nearby.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evening primroses produce nectar only when bees are nearby.
Scientists have long known that plants respond to many kinds of sound.
An experiment suggests that some flowers may respond to the sound of bees by making their nectar sweeter.
Bees prefer flowers that produce high-pitched sounds.
questions.correct: An experiment suggests that some flowers may respond to the sound of bees by making their nectar sweeter.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text centers on the experiment in which bee sounds led flowers to make sweeter nectar.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Imani has moved from a large city to a small farming town.

In the city, Imani had never noticed the sky; buildings had cut it into narrow strips. Here it was everywhere, and it was never the same twice. In her first weeks she kept a notebook of it—pale green at the edge of a storm, a flat white like paper in winter, a red so deep at sunset that she stopped her bicycle on the road to look. She had expected to be bored in the town. Instead she found she had something new to watch every evening.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Imani misses the tall buildings of the city where she used to live.
Imani is frightened by the storms in the farming town.
Imani finds unexpected interest in her new surroundings by observing the changing sky.
Imani wants to become a painter after she moves to the town.
questions.correct: Imani finds unexpected interest in her new surroundings by observing the changing sky.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

She expected boredom but discovers the ever-changing sky, which she records and watches each evening.

questions.question:
The following text is from a speech delivered at the opening of a public library. The speaker argues that libraries serve people of every age and background.

“This building will belong to the student preparing for an exam and to the grandmother learning to use a computer. It will belong to the new arrival practicing a new language and to the child hearing a story for the first time. Its doors will be open to all of them.”

Which quotation from the text most effectively illustrates the speaker's claim?
options: “the student preparing for an exam and … the grandmother learning to use a computer”
“hearing a story for the first time”
questions.correct: “the student preparing for an exam and … the grandmother learning to use a computer”
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The student and the grandmother show people of very different ages using the library.

questions.question:
A school district moved its start time from 7:30 to 8:30 and surveyed students about their sleep. A district report notes that students in most grades slept more after the change, though the effect was much smaller for students in grade 12, whose average sleep rose only from ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Grade 12 went from 6.4 to 6.6 hours, a gain of only 0.2 hours.

questions.question:
Glaciologist Ingrid Solberg has measured Tarn Glacier for decades. She reports that the glacier did not just shrink between 1960 and 2020; it shrank faster over time, losing ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: only about 0.2 kilometers of length from 1960 to 1980 but about 2.4 kilometers from 1980 to 2020.
about 0.2 kilometers of length from 1980 to 2020.
about 8.4 kilometers of length from 1960 to 2020.
the same amount of length in each decade from 1960 to 2020.
questions.correct: only about 0.2 kilometers of length from 1960 to 1980 but about 2.4 kilometers from 1980 to 2020.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A small loss in the first twenty years and a much larger loss afterward shows the shrinking sped up.

questions.question:
A school board is considering adopting a new reading program in every school. A board member argues that the program appears to be effective, citing results from three schools: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: Ashford had an average reading gain of 14 points.
Brookside did not use the program and had an average reading gain of 6 points.
the two schools that used the program had average reading gains of 14 and 13 points, while the school that did not use it had a gain of 6 points.
Cedar Hill had a smaller average reading gain than Ashford did.
questions.correct: the two schools that used the program had average reading gains of 14 and 13 points, while the school that did not use it had a gain of 6 points.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice compares schools with and without the program.

questions.question:
Lake Varn is home to two species of small fish that eat insects. Ecologist Rosa Lind noticed that where only one of the species lives, it feeds both near the surface and near the bottom of the lake. Where both species live together, however, one feeds almost entirely near the surface and the other almost entirely near the bottom. These observations suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: each species prefers insects found near the bottom of the lake.
one species will eventually replace the other in all parts of the lake.
insects near the surface of the lake are more nutritious than insects near the bottom.
when the two species share a habitat, they may divide the available food sources to avoid competing.
questions.correct: when the two species share a habitat, they may divide the available food sources to avoid competing.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Each species uses both zones when alone but splits them when together, which points to reduced competition.

questions.question:
Among the most popular exhibits at the science center ____________ a pendulum that shows the rotation of Earth and a room where visitors can experience simulated earthquakes.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The subject comes after the verb: “a pendulum … and a room,” a compound subject, so the verb is plural.

questions.question:
Some of the most detailed early maps of the night sky were made by astronomers at the observatory in Samarkand, which was built in the ____________ by the ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

No punctuation belongs between “the 1420s” and the phrase “by the ruler …,” which completes the clause.

questions.question:
Having studied the migration routes of whales for decades, ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the pod's next surfacing was predicted by the biologist.
predicting where the pod would surface next was possible for the biologist.
it was possible for the biologist to predict where the pod would surface next.
the biologist was able to predict where the pod would surface next.
questions.correct: the biologist was able to predict where the pod would surface next.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The opening phrase describes the biologist, who must be the subject placed right after the comma.

questions.question:
Many plants that grow in poor soil have formed partnerships with ____________ fungi wrap around or enter the plants' roots and supply them with minerals in exchange for sugars.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A colon introduces the explanation of the partnership; a comma alone would create a comma splice.

questions.question:
The two scientists disagreed about how to interpret the data, but neither of ____________ doubted that the measurements themselves were accurate.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The object of the preposition “of” must be the object pronoun them.

questions.question:
The ship's log, which recorded the weather every four ____________ now one of the most valuable sources of information about the climate of the eighteenth century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The nonessential clause “which recorded …” must be closed with a comma before the main verb “is.”

questions.question:
Of all the routes up the mountain, the northern ridge is considered the ____________ because of its loose rock and sudden storms.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Comparing more than two routes requires the superlative adjective most dangerous.

questions.question:
The Wright brothers' first powered flight, in 1903, lasted just twelve seconds and covered about 37 meters. ____________ within six years they were making flights that lasted more than an hour.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Hour-long flights six years later contrast with the very short first flight.

questions.question:
The researchers expected that students who studied with music would remember less. ____________ the students who studied with quiet instrumental music remembered slightly more than those who studied in silence.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The result was the opposite of what the researchers expected.

questions.question:
Spiders spin silk for many purposes. They use it to build webs for catching prey, to wrap their eggs, and to make lines for climbing. ____________ some young spiders use long strands of silk to float through the air and travel to new areas.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Floating through the air is one more use of silk, added to the list.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
  • Some weather stations there have recorded almost no rain for years at a time.
  • Because the air is so dry and clear, many large telescopes have been built there.
  • Scientists have also tested equipment for Mars missions in the Atacama.
